newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Moribund Belgian bonds seen rangebound to end year.
newsitem.headline: Moribund Belgian bonds seen rangebound to end year.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which on Thursday ignored benign U.S. CPI and sales data to stick like glue to the coattails of German Bunds, are expected to remain quiet and rangebound for the rest of the year, traders said.
"Not much is happening. Volumes are very, very low," one trader said. "We are range trading following Bunds and look likely to stay that way to the New Year."
There was some limited volatility in the futures contracts, but even there the trading range was a narrow 27 basis points.
The benchmark 2006 OLO was becalmed throughout the day with virtually no change in the spread over Bunds.

The market was in part undermined by worries of a Japanese pullout out of U.S. assets. However, the action was limited to professionals, one trader said, with institutionals reluctant to sell for tax reasons and private investors sitting tight.

Sentiment was being torpedoed by uncertainty ahead of the three-day Dublin summit of European Union finance ministers and leaders. There are fears in the market over a watered-down, post-EMU stability pact, which could undermine convergence plays. "Investors are very cautious," said a trader.
"There will be a 'yes, but' to the stability pact, so that everything can be delayed," said another.
Traders said that after a period of consolidation the clear trend seemed to be down.

Technically, the market looked weak, others said. Support at 120.61 for the front-month bond future was broken, but 120.49 held. "A break below 120.44 will add to the short-term negative outlook," said one. Resistance was seen at around 120.79 and 120.90. The contract was eight basis points down at 120.56.
The yield on the 2006 OLO ended Thursday at the psychologically important 6.00 percent against Wednesday's 5.99, and the spread over Bunds was an unchanged 10 basis points.
